edges.description: Whether the cytopenias result from altered PSTPIP1 function in hematopoietic cells or from chronic inflammation has not been resolved.
Hyperphosphorylation of PSTPIP1 is the intermediate linking loss of phosphatase binding to increased pyrin binding.
Release of pyrin from autoinhibition is the proposed, not demonstrated, intermediate.
The authors infer that calprotectin secretion is regulated by the pyrin-PSTPIP1 axis; the intervening steps are unknown.
IL-1beta and MRP8/14 release are described as reinforcing each other.
Proposed contribution of zinc unavailability to growth failure; not demonstrated.
Chronic neutropenia is the presumed main contributor to recurrent and sometimes severe infections; the sources report both features but do not test the link.
